name: South Africa
note: South African estate administration plus curatorship of property: Administration of Estates Act 66 of 1965, Intestate Succession Act 81 of 1987 and Wills Act 7 of 1953, from the Department of Justice’s published copies. The Act’s curatorship is over property only — letters of curatorship authorise acts in respect of property and business, not personal or health decisions — and s 73 still cross-refers to the repealed Mental Health Act 1973, so the modern appointment route under the Mental Health Care Act 17 of 2002 is not recorded here. Health-care proxies, the statutory consent hierarchy and organ donation sit in Department of Health legislation that was not reachable for this entry, so those roles are still missing. Powers of attorney are common law and lapse on the grantor’s incapacity; no statutory enduring power exists.

roles.name: Curator (letters of curatorship)
roles.summary: South Africa’s statutory substitute decision maker for property. Nobody may administer another’s property as curator without letters of curatorship from the Master, and the letters themselves fix the authority — a single act, care of the property, full administration, or carrying on a business.

assigned.event: Curator nominated by will or written instrument, or the Master appoints one where there is no nomination, where an absentee owns property, or where a court could appoint

starts.event: On letters of curatorship being granted by the Master; without them no one may take care of or administer the property

ends.event: Removal from office, the removal provisions for executors applying to curators
Death of the person, when the estate passes to the executor

states.label: Letters granted; authority as the letters specify

transitions.event: Curator nominated by will or written instrument (s 72)
Master appoints where there is no nomination, or for an absentee’s property (s 73)
Letters of curatorship granted; the letters fix whether the curator may perform a particular act, take care of, administer, or carry on a business (ss 71, 76)
Removal from office, s 54 applying to curators through s 85
Death of the person; the estate passes to the executor (s 14)

roles.name: Executor testamentary
roles.summary: An executor nominated by will. Authority comes from the Master of the High Court issuing letters of executorship on written application, not from the will alone.

assigned.event: Nominated as executor by a will that has been registered and accepted in the office of the Master

starts.event: Master issues letters of executorship on written application

transitions.event: Nomination by a valid will (Wills Act s 2)

conditions: will registered and accepted by the Master

roles.name: Executor dative
roles.summary: Where nobody was nominated by will, or the nominee cannot be found or will not act, the Master appoints. On intestacy the estate then devolves under the Intestate Succession Act.

assigned.event: Master acts where there is no nomination, or the nominee's whereabouts are unknown, or they have died, are incapacitated or refuse to act

ends.event: Estate liquidated and distributed to those entitled

transitions.event: Master appoints on failure of nomination (s 18(1))
Distribution, on intestacy under the Intestate Succession Act s 1

roles.name: Estate dealt with without an executor
roles.summary: Where the estate is below the amount the Minister sets by notice in the Gazette, the Master may dispense with an executor altogether and direct how the estate is to be liquidated and distributed.

assigned.event: Master decides the estate falls under the Gazetted amount

starts.event: Master gives directions in place of appointing an executor

ends.event: Estate liquidated and distributed as directed

conditions: estate does not exceed the amount determined by the Minister by notice in the Gazette

transitions.event: Estate liquidated and distributed as directed

probateGrantName.note: Issued by the Master of the High Court rather than a court, both where an executor is nominated by will and where the Master appoints.

smallEstateWithoutGrant.note: The Master may dispense with an executor where the estate does not exceed an amount the Minister sets by notice in the Gazette. The Act itself does not state a figure, and the current notice was not retrieved, so no amount is recorded here.
